title: Tanzania in Figures 2022 — National Bureau of Statistics
text:
The National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) is the principal government agency responsible for the collection, analysis and dissemination of official statistics in Tanzania. According to the 2022 Population and Housing Census, the total population of the United Republic of Tanzania was approximately 61.7 million people, an increase from 44.9 million recorded in the 2012 census. Mainland Tanzania accounted for about 59.9 million and Zanzibar for about 1.9 million.

The census reported an average annual population growth rate of roughly 3.2 percent between 2012 and 2022. The sex ratio was reported at about 95 males per 100 females. Dar es Salaam remained the most populous region. These figures are the authoritative reference for planning, resource allocation and research in the country.

Agriculture continues to employ the majority of the labour force. NBS labour statistics indicate that a large share of employment remains in the informal and agricultural sectors, with services and industry growing in urban regions.

title: Household Budget Survey — Poverty and Consumption in Tanzania
text:
The Household Budget Survey (HBS) measures household consumption expenditure and is the basis for Tanzania's official poverty estimates. The basic-needs poverty line is derived from the cost of a food basket meeting a minimum caloric requirement plus an allowance for non-food essentials.

The survey found that the proportion of the population below the basic-needs poverty line declined over successive rounds, though rural poverty remained substantially higher than urban poverty. Consumption inequality, measured by the Gini coefficient, remained broadly stable. Sampling followed a stratified two-stage cluster design, with enumeration areas selected as primary sampling units.

Researchers using HBS microdata should note that consumption aggregates are adjusted for regional price differences using spatial price indices, and that survey weights must be applied for nationally representative estimates.

title: Maji na Afya Vijijini: Utafiti wa Upatikanaji wa Maji Safi (UDSM)
text:
Utafiti huu uliofanywa katika Chuo Kikuu cha Dar es Salaam ulichunguza uhusiano kati ya upatikanaji wa maji safi na salama na afya ya jamii katika maeneo ya vijijini nchini Tanzania. Utafiti ulitumia sampuli ya kaya 1,200 kutoka mikoa mitatu na kukusanya takwimu kwa njia ya dodoso na mahojiano.

Matokeo yalionyesha kuwa kaya zenye upatikanaji wa maji safi ndani ya mita 500 zilikuwa na viwango vya chini vya magonjwa ya kuhara kwa watoto walio chini ya miaka mitano. Dhana kuu ya utafiti ilikuwa kwamba umbali wa chanzo cha maji una uhusiano wa moja kwa moja na matukio ya magonjwa yatokanayo na maji.

Utafiti ulipendekeza uwekezaji zaidi katika miundombinu ya maji vijijini na elimu ya afya kwa jamii. Takwimu zilichambuliwa kwa kutumia mbinu za takwimu za ulinganishi ikiwemo chi-square na uchambuzi wa urejeleaji.

title: Smallholder Maize Yields and Fertilizer Adoption in Tanzania
text:
This thesis examines the determinants of maize productivity among smallholder farmers in Tanzania, with a focus on inorganic fertilizer adoption. Using a household survey of 800 farming households across four agro-ecological zones, the study estimates a production function and an adoption model.

The analysis finds that fertilizer adoption is positively associated with maize yield per hectare, but adoption rates remain low due to cost, distance to input markets, and limited access to credit. Extension contact and membership in farmer groups were significant predictors of adoption. The study applies a Cobb-Douglas specification and controls for rainfall and soil quality.

Policy recommendations include improving input subsidy targeting, strengthening rural credit access, and expanding agricultural extension services. Data limitations include potential recall bias in self-reported yields.

title: COSTECH National Research Priorities and Innovation Report
text:
The Tanzania Commission for Science and Technology (COSTECH) coordinates and promotes research and innovation across the country. Its national research priorities emphasise agriculture and food security, health, energy, water, industrialisation, and information and communication technology.

COSTECH supports researchers through competitive grants and maintains a national research registry. The report highlights the need to strengthen the link between academic research and industry, to increase the number of researchers per capita, and to improve open access to publicly funded research outputs.

The commission also stresses research integrity and the avoidance of predatory publishing, advising researchers to publish in indexed, peer-reviewed venues and to consult recognised journal quality indicators before submission.

title: Sekondari na Mitihani: Muhtasari wa Mtaala wa NECTA/CSEE
text:
Baraza la Mitihani la Taifa la Tanzania (NECTA) linasimamia mitihani ya kitaifa ikiwemo Mtihani wa Kidato cha Nne (CSEE). Mtaala wa elimu ya sekondari umegawanywa katika masomo ya lazima na ya hiari, ikijumuisha Hisabati, Kiingereza, Kiswahili, Baiolojia, Kemia, Fizikia, Jiografia na Historia.

Muhtasari wa somo la Hisabati unajumuisha maeneo ya namba, aljebra, jiometri, takwimu na uwezekano. Wanafunzi wanatakiwa kuelewa dhana za msingi za takwimu ikiwemo wastani, wastani wa kati (median), na mpangilio wa data kabla ya kuendelea na uchambuzi wa hali ya juu.

Upangaji wa madaraja katika CSEE hutumia mfumo wa alama unaobadilishwa kuwa madaraja A hadi F. Walimu wanashauriwa kuwaandaa wanafunzi kwa kuzingatia malengo ya somo yaliyoainishwa katika muhtasari rasmi.

title: Rapid Guaranteed Publication Journal of Multidisciplinary Science
text:
This journal offers rapid guaranteed publication within 72 hours upon payment of an article processing charge. We accept manuscripts from all fields with minimal peer review. Authors are guaranteed acceptance and immediate indexing.

Note for the Weave platform: this record is included deliberately as a NEGATIVE example. It matches predatory-publishing patterns (guaranteed rapid publication, pay-to-publish with minimal review) and is flagged accordingly so the citation-check tool and the researcher-mode guardrail can warn users before it is cited.

title: Tanzania Journal of Health Research — Malaria Prevalence Study
text:
This peer-reviewed study examines malaria prevalence among children under five in selected districts of Tanzania. Using rapid diagnostic tests on a sample of 2,400 children, the study estimates district-level prevalence and identifies associated risk factors.

The results show that insecticide-treated net usage is associated with significantly lower odds of infection, while proximity to stagnant water and lower household wealth quintiles are associated with higher odds. Logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios, controlling for age, sex and season.

The authors recommend sustained net distribution campaigns and targeted vector control in high-transmission districts. Ethical approval was obtained and informed consent recorded for all participants.
